name: Inner Dialogue
intro: Welcome. Today we're going to listen inward.
Inside each of us, there are many voices. The critic. The protector. The dreamer. The child.
Most of the time, they talk over each other. Or one drowns the rest out.
Right now, we're going to give each one a moment to speak.
You don't have to agree with any of them. Just listen.
Let's get quiet enough to hear.
body: First, notice which voice is loudest right now.
Is it the planner, listing everything that needs to be done?
Is it the worrier, running through worst-case scenarios?
Is it the critic, pointing out what you did wrong?
Don't silence it. Just acknowledge it. Say inwardly: I hear you.
Sometimes that's all a voice needs to quiet down.
Now look for a quieter voice. One that's been waiting.
It might be the part of you that's tired and needs rest.
Or the part that has a dream you've been ignoring.
Or the part that just wants to play, to laugh, to be light.
What does this voice want to say? Give it room.
There's a part of you that remembers being very young.
Before the armor. Before the masks. Before you learned what was acceptable.
What did that younger you love? What made them light up?
That child is still in you. Not as a memory. As a living presence.
What do they need from you today?
Now find the voice of your deepest wisdom. The one that speaks rarely but clearly.
It doesn't shout. It doesn't argue. It just knows.
If you asked it one question right now, what would you ask?
Sit in silence for a moment and wait for the answer.
It may come as words. Or a feeling. Or just a knowing.
All these voices are you. Not enemies. Not problems. Parts of a whole.
The critic is trying to protect you. The worrier is trying to prepare you.
The child is trying to remind you what joy feels like.
What if, instead of fighting them, you thanked them?
Thank you for trying to help. I've got it from here.
closing: You've just had a conversation with yourself. That's rare and valuable.
Most people never stop to listen to their own inner world.
You did. And whatever you heard, it matters.
Take a deep breath. All your voices are a little more at peace now.
Open your eyes. You know yourself a little better today.
